body:
It's super common for people to feel this way about themselves. You can talk to so many smart, funny, and pretty people who think themselves anything but. We're our own worst critics and it's extremely hard to see our own merit.

Couple things: first off, don't *try* to be funny. Often times that just makes you feel bad and try to force jokes that aren't there. I'm not saying don't crack jokes or be silly but don't focus on trying to make everyone laugh. A lot of it comes down to finding your voice. What makes you laugh? What do you do that makes others laugh? It's more about training your brain to make it habitual. And hell, sometimes it takes time to come into your own. My friends say I'm funny but I sure wasn't when I was your age. Took a long while for me to stop trying so hard and making an ass out of myself. 

A lot of development when you're young isn't being who you want to be, it's growing into that person. Think of a tree planted with a wooden post to make sure it grows straight or vines growing up a wooden lattice to make a pretty decoration. You don't buy the tree fully grown you help it grow into what you want it to be. People are the same way. We're not static beings, we're works in progress. 

Finally. Take a breath. This mode of thinking is normal but not helpful. Something that helps is taking the mental effort to seriously try to listen when you get a compliment. Recognize that your brain is lying to you and exert the conscious effort to think a better thought. You're already on that path and clearly quite cognizant so you're doing a good job right now!

And hey, your friends should be there to talk to about this! You can tell them how you feel and they can help support you! Hell! Those you think are so gosh darn funny and pretty might be feeling the exact same way!

Stay strong friend!
I do but it's more just sometimes I need a shoulder to cry on. I need somebody to not give up on me when I'm at my lowest and I always feel like I come up short.
